sentences.text: The genus Koutalisaurus, meaning "spoon lizard" due to the shape of its jaw, is known from a mostly complete dentary found in the Late Cretaceous Tremp Formation near Abella de la Conca, Spain. The dentary is very elongate with a long, toothless front portion bent steeply downward and inward, creating a spoon-like shape when complete.
The dentary is comparable in size to other hadrosaurids but is on the small side and possesses unusual proportions.

The holotype specimen, IPS SRA 27, was originally assigned to Pararhabdodon in 1999 before being reclassified as the new species Koutalisaurus kohlerorum by Prieto-Marquez et al. in 2006. The genus Koutalisaurus was named by Prieto-Marquez, Gaete, Rivas, Galobart, and Boada in 2006. The species Koutalisaurus kohlerorum was named by Prieto-Marquez et al. in 2006.
Koutalisaurus was later considered an invalid nomen dubium, though subsequent studies continue to treat it as a valid genus.

Prieto-Marquez et al. (2006) classified the animal as a hadrosaurid but noted its uncertain placement within the family. Koutalisaurus is classified within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae. Koutalisaurus belongs to the tribe Tsintaosaurini.

Recent work by Prieto-Marquez and Wagner suggests that Koutalisaurus is the same genus as Pararhabdodon, as originally hypothesized. A 2020 study by Nick Longrich and colleagues classified Koutalisaurus as an arenysaurin. The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Koutalisaurus as Arenysaurini.
Koutalisaurus kohlerorum lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian, approximately 70 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
